subject: Creativity
title: Reversal: Turning Problems Upside Down
description: A quick, practical guide to Reversal: Turning Problems Upside Down.

hook.text: Instead of asking 'How do we attract customers?' ask 'How would we guarantee losing every customer?' Then reverse it.

buildup.text: Reversal takes a problem statement and inverts it — solving the opposite reveals what you're currently doing wrong.

discovery.text: It works because the brain is better at identifying problems than solutions. Reversal harnesses this natural strength.

twist.text: Pre-mortem analysis uses this: 'Assume the project failed. Why?' Teams identify more risks than traditional planning.

climax.text: Toyota's 'Five Whys' combined with reversal produced the lean manufacturing revolution — eliminating waste by reversing.

punchline.text: Flip the question. The answer was hiding on the other side.

quiz.question: Why is reversal effective as a creative technique?
options: The brain is naturally better at identifying problems than solutions

details.summary: Reversal inverts a problem to examine it from the opposite direction. Instead of asking how to increase customer satisfaction, ask how to make customers as unhappy as possible. The reversed perspective reveals hidden assumptions and overlooked solutions.
details.whyItMatters: Reversal is surprisingly effective because it bypasses mental blocks. People who are stuck on a problem can often immediately list ways to make it worse, and those answers contain the seeds of real solutions.
takeaways: Invert the problem to see it from the opposite direction
Listing ways to worsen a situation reveals what actually matters
Reversal exposes hidden assumptions in the original framing

faq.question: How does thinking about making things worse help?
faq.answer: When people try to make something worse, they identify the critical factors that matter most. Reversing each negative factor back to positive often reveals solutions that were invisible when approaching the problem directly.

faq.question: When should you use the reversal technique?
faq.answer: Reversal works best when you are stuck on a problem and conventional approaches have failed. It is also useful early in a project to challenge assumptions about what the real problem is before committing to a direction.
